QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_18

question.text: 'Lotus Category II AIF' has negotiated AFFIRMATIVE rights in a start-up investee. Which of the following BEST describes an affirmative right?

answer.text: A corporate action that CANNOT be carried out without the AIF's express consent, even if an ordinary majority of 51% shareholders approves it
A right to receive first claim on exit proceeds
A right to convert debentures to equity at par value
A right to nominate the Statutory Auditor unilaterally

explanation.text: The Logic: Affirmative rights are investor approvals required regardless of shareholding — even if a matter would otherwise pass with an ordinary 51% majority, it cannot be effected without the affirmative-right holder's express consent. The workbook lists standard matters such as capital structure changes, MOA/AOA alteration, new debt, IPO decisions, M&A, ESOP changes, and changes to the board / Key Managerial Personnel. The Trap: "First claim on exit" describes a liquidation preference. "Debenture conversion at par" describes a hybrid-security conversion term. Unilateral auditor nomination is not how affirmative rights are framed in the workbook. Note: The workbook includes board / KMP appointment changes within the standard affirmative-right matters, so appointment rights are not categorically excluded — the defining feature is the consent requirement, not the subject area.
